topic: Rectangular all-resolution common-half-sum frontier for exact two-sided-market randomization inference. For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations B and S of sizes 2n_B and 2n_S, optimize F(a,b)=sum_l a_l b_l over covering paired rectangular partitions with at least R common half-sum assignments. For every R>=4, prove that when n_B,n_S>=4R every optimizer belongs to the explicit finite residual catalog C_R with residual totals at most 2R; derive the exact affine phase formula and all equality cases, and give certified finite enumeration below the threshold. Construct the constant-incidence Z-then-P sampler and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null using null-adjusted focal outcomes. Keep weak-null, two-sided-95-percent-at-R=20, power-optimality, and unrestricted-biclique claims out of scope. Consumer: Ye et al. Management Science 2023 Platform O experiment, which independently randomized unequal user-view and ad populations with balanced treatment/control within each experimental side. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A two-stage concentration proof was derived: a unit-residual benchmark forces buyer residual A<=R, and a support-preserving residual-copy competitor gives (n_B-2A+1)D<=(n_B-1)A and D<2A<=2R. Exact catalog, incidence, inversion, aspect-ratio, and threshold audits found no counterexample; small-margin universal uniqueness, raw-outcome conditioning, and ordinary two-sided 95-percent inversion at support 20 were checked and excluded. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify H(a,b')=H(a) for the residual-copy competitor and the positive-loss inequality without assuming an ordering of seller coordinates. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the 136 residual-copy checks and all 2,628 feasible C_4 targets at (n_B,n_S)=(16,17); any support-loss counterexample or outside-catalog optimizer stops the field launch. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_halfsum_orbit_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For independent uniform half-randomization of 2n_B buyers and 2n_S sellers, determine the exact maximum of F(a,b)=sum_l a_l b_l over covering paired rectangular partitions supporting at least R common half-sum assignments, and classify every maximizer by a finite residual catalog when n_B,n_S>=4R.

source_refs.claim: Their exact total-effect test uses equal square k-blocks, notes that diagonal blocks are unnecessary, and leaves block choice as a power heuristic rather than optimizing all valid rectangles.
source_refs.author: Jizhou Liu, Azeem M. Shaikh, Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: Biclique-based conditional randomization tests are exact under interference and larger conditioning bicliques improve power, but construction uses graph clustering rather than an exact product-slice classification.
source_refs.author: David Puelz, Guillaume Basse, Avi Feller, Panos Toulis
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: The Platform O study used a two-sided user-view/ad experiment to address cannibalization and motivates improved methodology for marketplace experiments.
source_refs.author: Zikun Ye, Dennis J. Zhang, Heng Zhang, Renyu Zhang, Xin Chen, Zhiwei Xu

source_refs.excerpt: without imposing overlap and without asserting an elementary closed-form classification.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nearest exact-inference paper establishes validity for chosen equal square blocks but analyzes the support-versus-focal-size tradeoff only for that construction; the general biclique literature supplies heuristic graph optimization rather than an extremal classification. The prior construction reduces a related design problem to orbit weights but explicitly stops before a closed-form classification. The rectangular destination instead has two coupled half-sum profiles. Its missing proof step is a support-preserving residual concentration argument that works simultaneously on both margins and tracks equality, including verification that residual copying preserves common-half-sum support without ordering seller coordinates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite theorem giving an explicit piecewise-affine optimum in (n_B,n_S,R), proving that every optimizer lies in a catalog C_R with residual totals at most 2R for n_B,n_S>=4R, listing all equality cases, and certifying every smaller margin by finite enumeration.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from two-sided marketplace interference to an imputable conditioning event and then to the focal-size/support tradeoff, replacing heuristic block selection with an exact rectangular frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: independent randomization on two market sides creates pair-level interference -> exact testing requires assignments sharing an imputable exposure pattern -> focal size and randomization support compete -> determine the complete rectangular efficiency frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Represent subset-sum profiles through pure extremal objects, bound their bilinear pairing, and propagate equality conditions through the purification argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its central object is a bilinear pairing of two subset-sum profiles, structurally matching sum_l a_l b_l, although fixed-cardinality common-half-sum and covering constraints are new.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate imputability into a biclique of the null-exposure graph, prove conditional-test validity, and relate both biclique dimensions to power.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested rectangle objective is an analytically structured specialization of their focal-units-by-assignments biclique tradeoff.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a constant-incidence Z-then-P sampler for every catalogued optimal rectangular conditioning event under unequal buyer and seller population sizes, and prove that its law equals independent half-randomization conditional on that event.

source_refs.claim: Their efficient block permutation sampler relies on equal-shaped blocks, while sampling arbitrary nonsymmetric conditional randomization laws is described as computationally challenging.
source_refs.author: Jizhou Liu, Azeem M. Shaikh, Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: Exact permutation tests for randomized group formation follow by proving that design symmetries propagate to exposure through equivariance and conditioning on group-action orbits.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Basse, Peng Ding, Avi Feller, Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: A two-stage mirror-allocation sampler preserves unbiasedness and exact Fisher inference for symmetric rerandomization criteria.
source_refs.author: Per Johansson, Mårten Schultzberg
source_refs.venue: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics

source_refs.excerpt: Conditional independence of the two assignment waves therefore gives conditional independence

open_problems.why_unsolved: Uniformly permuting identical blocks works because every admissible assignment has the same orbit multiplicity, while the prior cross-wave argument relies on conditionally independent product-Bernoulli fields. Rectangular catalog elements can have different shapes and residual types on the two market sides, so naive independent permutation may overweight assignments admitting more compatible partitions. The missing proof is a fiber-counting identity: after selecting a common half-sum pattern Z, every admissible assignment must occur in the same number of compatible partition/permutation objects P.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit Z-then-P algorithm and a fiber-counting theorem proving constant incidence over every admissible buyer-seller assignment, hence equality with the intended conditional randomization law and finite-sample exactness of Monte Carlo p-values.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its operational focus on sampling the correct conditional law and its contrast between easy symmetric permutations and difficult general conditional sampling.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: conditional randomization validity depends on the exact assignment law -> richer rectangles enlarge the focal set -> unequal shapes destroy the obvious uniform permutation law -> constant incidence restores implementable exact inference

method_exemplars.technique: Represent permutations by a group action, condition on an orbit, and prove through equivariance that design invariance transfers to exposure invariance and exact p-values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The P-stage is an orbit randomization, and its required constant-incidence lemma is the rectangular analogue of the paper's equivariance argument.

method_exemplars.technique: Pair allocations with their mirrors in a two-stage restricted sampler and prove that equal assignment representation retains unbiasedness and exact Fisher testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both constructions certify the target randomization law by arranging equal representation after a first-stage restriction.

open_problems.open_problem: Under the sharp constant total-effect model Y_ij(1,1)=Y_ij(0,0)+tau, establish exact one-sided randomization-test inversion for catalogued rectangular conditioning events using null-adjusted focal outcomes, including the endpoint rule for the discrete p-value function.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves finite-sample validity for the sharp zero total-effect null on k-block focal pairs but does not derive interval inversion for a nonzero constant total effect.
source_refs.author: Jizhou Liu, Azeem M. Shaikh, Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: Fisher-test inversion requires explicit treatment of discrete p-value functions; the paper gives guaranteed-coverage inversion rules and Monte Carlo control for randomized experiments.
source_refs.author: Xiaokang Luo, Tirthankar Dasgupta, Minge Xie, Regina Y. Liu
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: A conditional randomization test under interference is exact when its conditioning mechanism makes the tested potential outcomes imputable over every retained assignment.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Basse, Avi Feller, Panos Toulis

open_problems.why_unsolved: The zero-effect null allows observed focal outcomes to be reused directly, whereas inversion at tau!=0 requires subtracting the hypothesized effect according to each pair's joint exposure even though the focal set and allowed assignments were selected from the observed two-sided assignment. The missing steps are assignment-by-assignment imputability of the adjusted focal array and monotonicity of the selected one-sided statistic's discrete p-value. General Fisher-inversion results supply endpoint machinery but not these dyadic-exposure and conditioning arguments.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-population theorem proving imputability of the null-adjusted statistic over every retained rectangle assignment, monotonicity of the one-sided p-value in tau, and exact 1-alpha coverage of the generalized-inverse confidence ray, including a valid Monte Carlo implementation.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its presentation of test inversion as a nontrivial finite-sample problem caused by discrete randomization distributions, specialized to two-sided focal conditioning.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fisher tests give exact point-null inference -> scientific use requires effect-size intervals -> discrete p-value functions make naive inversion ambiguous -> prove valid one-sided inversion for the rectangular two-sided design

method_exemplars.technique: Treat Fisher p-values as a confidence distribution, prove monotonicity and coverage conditions, and define generalized-inverse endpoints for a discrete p-value curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After two-sided imputability is established, the requested deliverable is precisely a discrete randomization-test inversion theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Formalize a conditioning mechanism and prove finite-sample validity by checking statistic imputability for every retained focal-unit and assignment pair.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Null-adjusted focal outcomes must satisfy this exact condition before inversion can be invoked.

open_problems.open_problem: For independent complete randomization with arbitrary fixed treated counts I_1!=I/2 and J_1!=J/2, characterize the optimal covering rectangular conditioning events at support floor R, or identify sharply the regimes where no bounded-residual affine catalog analogous to the half-randomized case exists.

source_refs.claim: The general design permits arbitrary fixed treated counts, but its focal-size/support calculation and power illustration specialize to square populations with half of each side treated.
source_refs.author: Jizhou Liu, Azeem M. Shaikh, Panos Toulis

source_refs.claim: In two-sided marketplaces, treatment proportions affect bias and variance differently, creating an operationally relevant bias-variance tradeoff.
source_refs.author: Hannah Li, Geng Zhao, Ramesh Johari, Gabriel Y. Weintraub

source_refs.claim: Away from probability one half, subset-sum concentration maximizers can have strongly unbalanced sign patterns, so complement symmetry is not innocuous.
source_refs.author: Mihir Singhal

open_problems.why_unsolved: Half randomization pairs feasible assignments by complementation and converts admissibility into a common half-sum condition. Arbitrary treated counts destroy that involution: the sides require matched fixed-cardinality subset sums and rectangular fibers can receive unequal weights. Singhal shows that even one-profile concentration changes its optimizer away from one half, but does not solve the coupled fixed-cardinality product objective. Thus the first proof step that fails is the symmetry reduction preceding the residual-copy argument.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem indexed by (I,I_1,J,J_1,R) giving the exact rectangular focal-size frontier and all equality cases in explicit allocation-ratio regimes, or a counterexample theorem identifying the first ratios and margins where a bounded-residual affine catalog fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its practical bias-variance account of why platforms deliberately choose non-half treatment proportions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: market interference biases ordinary experiments -> randomized side and treatment fraction are design levers -> non-half fractions can be operationally preferable -> exact rectangular inference needs a frontier beyond complement-symmetric half assignment

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose positive and negative subset-sum profiles into pure objects, exploit bilinearity, and use Fourier analysis to locate extremal imbalances when half-probability symmetry is absent.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem similarly must replace complement symmetry with an extremal analysis of two coupled asymmetric subset-sum profiles.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on focal rectangles preserving treated counts and prove exactness through the induced conditional assignment law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The paper already defines arbitrary treated-count two-sided complete randomization; the missing component is the exact optimal construction and sampler.

literature_map:
1. Ye et al. (2023, Management Science, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2022.4550) supply the application anchor: Platform O used a two-sided user-view/ad experiment to control cannibalization.
2. Johari, Li, Liskovich, and Weintraub (2022, Management Science, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2021.4247; arXiv:2002.05670) show that two-sided randomization mitigates marketplace-interference bias across market-balance extremes.
3. Li, Zhao, Johari, and Weintraub (2021, arXiv:2104.12222) show that treatment fractions create a bias-variance tradeoff, motivating theory beyond a single allocation proportion.
4. Bajari et al. (2023, Statistical Science, DOI 10.1214/23-STS883) formalize marketplace experiments with multiple randomization layers and explain why ordinary one-population RCT logic is inadequate.
5. Masoero et al. (2026, JRSSB, DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf073; arXiv:2401.01264) derive estimators and CLTs under multiple randomization designs but do not optimize exact-test conditioning support.
6. Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026 revision, arXiv:2504.06215) are the closest anchor: their k-block total-effect test is exact, but the square half-treated support calculation yields only heuristic block selection.
7. Liu et al. note that diagonal blocks are unnecessary, unequal or indivisible cases are cumbersome, and sampling general conditional laws is challenging.
8. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12478; arXiv:1910.10862) connect imputable conditioning events to bicliques and power but use graph-clustering constructions rather than an exact product-slice frontier.
9. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asy072; arXiv:1709.08036) provide the conditioning-mechanism and imputability theorem required assignment by assignment.
10. Athey, Eckles, and Imbens (2018, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2016.1241178; arXiv:1506.02084) are the foundational artificial-experiment anchor for exact tests of nonsharp interference hypotheses.
11. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA20134; arXiv:1904.02308) use group actions, orbit conditioning, and equivariance to obtain efficient exact permutation tests.
12. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021, JRSSB, DOI 10.1111/rssb.12429; arXiv:2004.08472) show that inversion of discrete Fisher p-value functions requires explicit conditions and provide guaranteed-coverage endpoint machinery.
13. Johansson and Schultzberg (2020, JCGS, DOI 10.1080/10618600.2020.1753531) show how a two-stage mirror-allocation sampler preserves exact inference under restricted randomization.
14. Harshaw et al. (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1214/23-EJS2111; arXiv:2103.06392) and Pouget-Abadie et al. (2019, NeurIPS) optimize precision in bipartite experiments under modeled exposures, contrasting with the proposed model-free sharp-null frontier.
15. Singhal (2019, arXiv:1912.02886) supplies the closest additive-combinatorial machinery through bilinear subset-sum profiles, but the scan found no coupled common-half-sum rectangular classification.
